text:
Sam Carter: Heads-up — p99 TTFT in eu-west2 climbed from ~120ms to ~520ms starting ~10:15 UTC. Grafana shows tokens/sec steady but request queue depth rising on several inference shards. https://grafana.redwood/internal/d/ttft/eu-west2
Priya Nair: Confirming, logs show a bump in egress ECONNRESET from nat-gateway on pool-7 around the same time. Small burst of 502s to model-backend instances.
Marco Li: Can we get a quick PromQL to slice by instance and quantify queueing vs execution? Trying:```
histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(ttft_seconds_bucket{region="eu-west2"}[5m])) by (le,instance))
```
Sam Carter: Thx — ran that, here's a grep from the tail of the shard logs (pool-7):```
[2026-03-18T10:16:02Z] shard=pool-7 inst=i-0abc123 req=xyz ttft=0.48s status=502 net_err="connection reset by peer"
[2026-03-18T10:16:05Z] shard=pool-7 inst=i-0def456 req=abc ttft=0.51s status=200
```
sre-bot: ALERT: EU-WEST2 token-ttft-p99 breached 350ms (currently 520ms) — triggered 4m ago. Incident INC-5483 created.
Jules (oncall): @Jules here — can someone run tcptraceroute from one of the affected nodes to the egress NAT IP and paste results? quick command:```
sudo tcptraceroute -n -w 3 <nat-ip> 443
```
Priya Nair: Running that now on i-0abc123, results look like a hop delay spike at hop 4 (~300ms) and then occasional retransmits. Also opening provider ticket, referencing INC-5483.
Marco Li: In parallel we should reduce in-flight batch sizes for pool-7 to reduce queuing pressure. Suggest config change: batch_max_tokens  = 6 (was 8) and enable per-shard backpressure. I'll create a canary rollout to 10% of pool-7.
Sam Carter: Good plan. For immediate mitigation, I've added a temporary routing rule to divert new requests from pool-7 to pool-9 (same region) until nat ticket resolves. Monitoring dashboards updated.
Priya Nair: I've prepared a small canary patch:```
- name: reduce-batch-pool7
  patch: |
    shards: pool-7
    config:
      batch_max_tokens: 6
      batch_flush_interval_ms: 8
```
I'll push in 2m and watch p99.
Marco Li: Also recommending alert tuning: current p99 alert is static at 350ms, but we're seeing noisy network-induced spikes. I'll open PR to change to a rolling window + increase to 450ms and add an annotation to call out network errors as likely cause. PR: https://git.redwood/infra/alerts/pulls/298
Jules (oncall): After the routing change + canary, p99 dropped to ~190ms for new traffic. Still seeing occasional blips for existing inflight requests. Good rollback plan if things worsen: revert routing + restore batch size.
Sam Carter: Closing loop — cloud provider acknowledged NAT scaling issue and applied a fix, provider says it should stabilize in ~15m. Leaving INC-5483 open for post-mortem.
Priya Nair: Post-mortem action items: 1) add nat saturation monitoring and alert, 2) implement per-pool egress capacity soft-limits, 3) document knob for rapid batch-size canary. Assigning tasks.
Marco Li: I'll update the Grafana dashboard panels to include nat-gateway 5xxs and a queue-depth overlay so the correlation is clearer.
Sam Carter: thanks all. :thumbsup:
